body:
### Summary

When using the `--active` flag with the script interface, uv will treat `$VIRTUAL_ENV` as the script's environment, and provided it doesn't find a usable Python environment there, it will delete everything in the directory before creating a new virtual env in its place. It does this whenever the directory is not recognized as a virtual environment (i.e. there's no `pyvenv.cfg` file), which includes normal directories, as well as conda environments with incompatible Python versions.

The project interface does correctly protect against this scenario, and refuses to go ahead. 

Worse still, there's no user-facing indication that anything got removed, you would have to run the command with the `-v` flag to notice, which also shows that uv recognizes that it is an invalid environment, but still goes ahead removing and recreating it as if it were.

```
$ VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/target uv run -v --active --script script.py
...
DEBUG Using active virtual environment `target` instead of script environment `/Users/casch/.cache/uv/environments-v2/script-1253798182c3d46b`
DEBUG Checking for Python environment at: `target`
WARN Ignoring existing script environment: Invalid environment at `target`: missing Python executable at `target/bin/python3`
...
DEBUG Removed virtual environment at: target
DEBUG Creating script environment at: target
...
```

This is important because pointing the `$VIRTUAL_ENV` variable to a conda prefix is the workaround suggested for #11315 and as mentioned before, conda environments don't have a `pyvenv.cfg` file. 

Here's an example:

```
$ mkdir -p target/subdir && echo "very important data" > target/important.txt
$ cat > script.py <<'EOF'
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = []
# ///
print("the script ran, but at what cost?")
EOF

$ VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/target uv run --active --script script.py
the script ran, but at what cost?

$ ls target
.gitignore  .lock  CACHEDIR.TAG  bin  lib  pyvenv.cfg
```

Now `important.txt` and `subdir/` are gone.

The same happens with `uv sync --script script.py --active`

As a comparison, the project interface refuses. This needs a `pyproject.toml` to get past project discovery.
```
$ mkdir -p target/subdir && echo "important data" > target/important.txt

$ printf '[project]\nname = "proj"\nversion = "0.1.0"\nrequires-python = ">=3.11"\ndependencies = []\n' > pyproject.toml

$ VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/target uv sync --active
error: Project virtual environment directory `/Users/casch/Projects/open-source/target` cannot be used because it is not a valid Python environment (no Python executable was found)
```

`ScriptEnvironment::get_or_init` calls `uv_fs::remove_virtualenv(&root)` unconditionally, see,
https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/7896d580c245493c88ea5be56724e6e42ee7d197/crates/uv/src/commands/project/mod.rs#L2229

`remove_virtualenv` itself doesn't check that the target is a virtual environment, it only defers deleting `pyvenv.cfg` until last.
The project path avoids this issue by doing the check separately before calling `remove_virtualenv`.

I think that the check would be better inside `remove_virtualenv` instead of having each caller do the check separately, which also lines up with the ethos of #14985 

I'd be happy to work on this if you'd like, but obviously I'd like confirmation that this would be the correct solution, given that so many places call that function.


### Platform

Darwin 25.5.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.12.7 (Homebrew 2026-08-27 aarch64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

Python 3.13.13
title: `uv run --active --script` deletes the contents of a non-virtual-environment `VIRTUAL_ENV`
